description: There is no `# renovate:` annotation in defaults/main.yml and no `//patch-automerge` extend here, because there is no version of YaCy for Renovate to bump. YaCy's upstream stopped publishing versioned container image tags: everything docker.io/yacy/yacy_search_server carries today is `latest`, `latest-ubuntu`, `latest-alpine`, two `sha-f4509ae2...` tags from June 2025, the frozen `last-solr-8-11-2`, the abandoned `aarch64-latest` and `armv7-latest`, and a single `1.93` last pushed on 2024-05-19. The role points `yacy_version` at `latest` for that reason, and an annotation on a floating tag would either match nothing or make Renovate chase `latest` around in circles.

The practical consequence is worth spelling out for whoever reads this next: the deployed version of YaCy is not pinned by this role at all. The installation tasks pull the image on every playbook run, so an operator's YaCy moves to whatever upstream last built - the image rebuilt on 2026-08-20 reports itself as 1.942, while the newest git tag upstream carries is Release_1.941. Renovate can neither improve nor worsen that. Should upstream ever start publishing versioned tags again, this is the file that grows a `# renovate: datasource=docker depName=yacy/yacy_search_server` annotation on the `yacy_version:` line, and bin/compute-next-tag.sh already switches from carrying the version over to deriving it.

Even with a version to track, patch-automerge would be the wrong call here. YaCy keeps an embedded Solr index on disk under `yacy_data_path`, and that index is upgraded in place with no way back: the image ships Solr 9.10.1 on Lucene 9.12.3, Lucene reads one major format back through lucene-backward-codecs and refuses to write an older one, and upstream published a `last-solr-8-11-2` image tag precisely so that operators could stand still before the Solr 8 to 9 jump rewrote their index. A fresh-install Molecule scenario, however thorough, structurally cannot see that risk - it never has an old index to migrate.

Everything else Renovate manages here (GitHub Actions, prek hooks, mise tools, the Molecule pip requirements, the Ansible roles and collections, .python-version) is covered by the shared preset and keeps automerging on a branch.
